transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes (scheduled 45)
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Crestline Head of Data), Aman Patel (Crestline Platform Eng), Sophie Lin (Crestline Procurement)

Auto-generated summary: quick console walkthrough with emphasis on per-route cost and usage analytics. Pilot discussed.

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, and with me is Priya, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
00:06 Marta: Doing well, thanks. We wanted to see the console specifically — the per-route dashboards, token cost breakdown, things we can use for chargeback across teams.
00:12 Priya: Great, that's exactly what we'll walk through. I'll share my screen in a sec. Quick qual — what's your current traffic pattern and models?
00:20 Marta: Right now we use a mix — OpenAI for chat generative stuff and a homegrown embeddings pipeline. Peak is about 60 RPS for short chat, average token length ~250, but some routes hit 1k tokens. We're evaluating Redwood to get better cost predictability and on-prem options for PII-sensitive flows.
00:38 Jordan: Got it. And who owns success here? Is it Marta for ML and Aman for infra?
00:43 Marta: Yes, Aman will own infra integration, and Sophie will help on procurement/contract.
00:47 Sophie: Correct. We'll need procurement timeline later on.
00:50 Priya: Ok I'll pull up the Console. First page is the Usage Analytics overview — high level cost and token trends over time. You can see daily token volume, avg latency, and cost per 1k tokens.
01:05 (screen share noise)
01:10 Priya: Here's the per-route dashboard — each API route we host shows request count, p95 latency, and importantly token-level cost breakdown. You can group by model, region, and route tag.
01:22 Aman: Can we tag by environment? We have staging/prod and teams.
01:25 Priya: Yes, you can set route tags and the dashboard will break down costs by tag. That's what we use for internal chargeback.
01:30 Marta: The token-cost column — is that a real-time calc? How granular?
01:35 Priya: It's near-real-time; we compute cost per response using the model profile (tokens in/out * per-token unit cost) plus any infra surcharge. You can see historical bills and export CSVs.
01:44 Jordan: Also note we surface batching and cache savings estimates — if you enable KV cache or prefix caching you'll see projected token savings per route.
01:51 Aman: You said KV cache? We have a weird cache term in our notes — is that the same as K-V?
01:55 Priya: Yes KV cache — sometimes the transcription shows "case cache" — sorry, it's key-value cache for prefixes and reuse.
02:01 Marta: Ok. Curious about dedicated vs hosted: if we go dedicated reserved capacity, how does the console change for cost visibility?
02:08 Priya: Good q. For Dedicated you still get the same per-route dashboards; cost model shows committed vs burstable usage and amortized GPU costs. We show cost per token using your reserved commit so chargeback is accurate.
02:20 Aman: And for Private VPC/on-prem? We need to keep PII within our network and integrate KMS.
02:26 Priya: For Private, Console can be run in your VPC with a private control plane. You keep keys in your KMS/HSM. We still surface the same dashboards; some infra-level metrics are collected by a local agent.
02:36 Marta: How do rollouts and fallbacks appear? We have higher-priority routes that need failover to smaller models if latency spikes.
02:42 Priya: We support canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies. The routing policy page shows policies per route — e.g., prefer low-latency region, then fall back to cheaper model variant. The dashboards will show whenever a fallback happened, with counts and associated cost delta.
02:59 Jordan: For cost modeling, we usually ask for a sample traffic profile. Aman, would you be able to share a week of anonymized traces?
03:05 Aman: I can, yeah. We can pull request per-minute RPS and token distribution. We'll need to scrub any PII.
03:11 Priya: That's perfect — we'll run a quick cost projection and a suggested config: batching size, quantization profile, and caching rules.
03:18 Marta: Security — do you have SOC 2 and ISO reports? Also audit logs, SSO integration?
03:23 Jordan: Yes SOC 2 Type II and ISO are in our security pack. We support SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit trails, and KMS integrations. Priya will share the package after the call.
03:33 Sophie: On procurement, what's typical contract length for Dedicated? We prefer 12 months but want flexibility.
03:38 Jordan: Standard is 12 or 24 month commits for Dedicated. For pilot we can do month-to-month Hosted credits and then move to a reserved commit if the pilot proves out.
03:46 (slight overlap) Aman: Latency targets — can you hit sub-100ms p95 for 256-token responses on the standard hosted nodes?
03:53 Priya: On hosted with optimized models we can hit sub-100 p95 for small seq lengths; for consistent sub-100 you might want Dedicated and region proximity. Also kernel selection and compilation change performance — our runtime picks optimized kernels per model/shard.
04:10 Marta: Any mis-transcriptions or vendor names we should be aware of — we sometimes see weird model names.
04:15 Priya: Yeah the console shows model catalog with Redwood-verified performance profiles so you can compare throughput/latency/cost.
04:22 Jordan: Let's jump into a demo route. (clicks) Here is "checkout-assist" route — you can see token distribution, top prompts, and cost by model.
04:33 Priya: Note the right-hand panel — cost breakdown: model token cost, infra amortized, and caching savings. You can adjust cost allocation rules to attribute infra to teams or routes.
04:45 Marta: Nice. Can we export per-route bills to our finance system?
04:48 Priya: Yep CSV export and API endpoint for usage data. You can also integrate with our cost export to BigQuery or S3.
04:55 Sophie: Procurement will want a sample invoice and SLOs for uptime.
04:59 Jordan: We'll include an example billing export and SLA doc in the follow-up.
05:03 Aman: For the pilot, what are typical observability hooks? We need traces, token-level logs, and request IDs tied to our tracing system.
05:11 Priya: We have tracing hooks and can send spans to your trace system, plus token-level cost logs and request IDs. Audit logs are retained per your plan.
05:19 Marta: Any gotchas — e.g., the console shows estimated batching savings but in practice is that accurate?
05:24 Priya: It's an estimate based on your request correlation and model characteristics. We'll run a bench with your traces to validate and tune batching thresholds. That's part of the pilot.
05:32 Jordan: Competitors — feels free to ask — people ask about OpenAI/Anthropic or Bedrock. The differentiator here is unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private and the cost tooling.
05:45 Marta: We heard about model quantization recommendations — can the console suggest quantization for routes?
05:51 Priya: Yes, Optimize suggests quantization profiles per workload balancing quality and cost. We tie evals to prompt sets so you can flag regressions.
06:00 Aman: Great. For network and certs — we need to know the TLS termination and whether we can use our private certs in the VPC deploy.
06:07 Priya: You can bring your certs in Private deployment; for Hosted we terminate at our edge and can do a mutual TLS option. We'll include details in the architecture notes.
06:16 Sophie: Timeline: procurement needs 2 weeks to review agreements. If pilot begins next week, we can review terms in parallel.
06:22 Jordan: That's fine. We'll send the pilot terms and a draft contract.
06:26 (brief pause, screen gestures)
06:30 Priya: Last bit — per-route alerting. You can set cost alerts, quota alerts, and latency SLO alerts. Those trigger webhooks or page ops.
06:39 Marta: Can alerts be scoped to tenant/team?
06:41 Priya: Yes — RBAC and alert scoping are supported.
06:45 Jordan: Awesome. Quick recap and next steps then.
06:48 Jordan: Action items: Jordan will send pricing and pilot proposal by Thu 5/21; Priya will share security docs and architecture notes by Wed 5/20; Aman will provide anonymized traffic by Fri 5/22. We'll schedule a 1-hour pilot kickoff/benchmark for Tue 5/26.
07:03 Sophie: Sounds good, procurement will review the example invoice.
07:07 Marta: Thanks for the walkthrough, helpful to see cost line items per route.
07:10 Jordan: Thanks all. We'll follow up in email with the materials.
07:14 (call ends)

Notes about transcription quality: medium — some technical terms mis-transcribed (KV cache -> case cache), occasional speaker label confusion.
